identity.title: Functional Dissection of cis-Regulatory Elements Controlling the Rice Florigen Gene RFT1.

content.abstract: The florigen gene RFT1 plays a critical role in regulating flowering time under artificial long-day (LD) conditions and functions prior to another florigen gene, Hd3a, under natural conditions in temperate regions of rice cultivation. Thus, RFT1 is important for the adaptation of rice to temperate areas of Asia. Compared with Hd3a, RFT1 is less strongly repressed under LD conditions. However, the cis-regulatory mechanisms governing RFT1 expression remain poorly understood. Here, we generated a series of CRISPR-Cas9 deletion mutants spanning an approximately 10 kb noncoding region surrounding RFT1. Expression and heading-date analyses identified multiple functional cis-regulatory regions involved in RFT1 activation. Combined analyses using mutants of the upstream Ghd7 regulator and Ehd1-overexpressing lines demonstrated that these regions function downstream of Ehd1 and Ghd7. Further fine-scale deletion and transient reporter assays revealed the importance of two Ehd1-binding sites among many candidate sites. Our results support a multilayered cis-regulatory architecture at the RFT1 locus and suggest evolutionary divergence in the regulation of FT orthologs between rice and Arabidopsis, as canonical CORE and CCAAT motifs appear to play only limited roles in RFT1 regulation. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic basis for the quantitative tuning of flowering time in rice cultivated in temperate regions.
